id: Terror Of The Deep Album Release! With Spirit Level-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Terror Of The Deep Album Release! With Spirit Level
long_description:
From the viscous psych-rock of Airport Underneath the Dome to the lavish, prog-rock inspired Space Epic, Terror Of The Deep have charted the depths of our oceans and the outer reaches of our solar system with a dedicated following in NZ and overseas. Consisting of Taipua Adams (bass), William Daymond (drums), Tom Watson (keys) and Oliver Dixon (guitar and lead vocal), the band were named by New York-based culture website Flavourwire as one of the ‘10 Great New Zealand Bands You Should Know’. To celebrate the fifteenth anniversary of its initial release, Terror of the Deep are proud to present their sophomore album ‘Permanent Weekend’ on limited-edition, hand numbered vinyl. Pressed at Mobineko in Taiwan on 140gm black vinyl, the original 11 song album has been given a fresh remaster and a new running order for this release. Each copy also contains a full colour insert featuring photos, posters, set lists, and reviews from when the album was first released in October 2011. LPs will be available to purchase at the gig.
-
Spirit Level is a new duo of long time sonic voyagers, Daniel Beban (guitar) and Andy Wright (drums). Plucking notes from the void, Dan employs an electric 12-string through a vintage Italian echo device and two classic NZ amps, creating crystalline layers of shifting harmonies and frozen peals of bell-like melodies that hover over Andy's playfully intricate summoning of interstellar energy.


Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

id: Sulfate - And It Wants - Album Release Tour-Meow, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Sulfate - And It Wants - Album Release Tour
long_description:
With Support Acts: Teeth & Birdparty

Feral, devolved and running on instinct, the six songs on Sulfate’s third album ‘And It Wants’ grapple between David Harris unleashing on his drum kit, Zac Arnold conjuring fuzz and feedback and Peter Ruddell’s taut, wiry guitar-work and commanding baritone. Written and recorded in New Lynn’s industrial area, this new batch of songs were created on a diet of Cormac McCarthy novels, Adam Curtis documentaries and the madness of gothic horror. Since recording, Sulfate's line up has expanded once more, introducing multi-instrumentalist Louisa Nicklin to the band's inexorable live performances.


Sonically, Sulfate set out some parameters at the outset of the album recordings - and it was important for things to sound real. The band wanted real instruments to be played, and, importantly, sound like they’re being played, by real, living people. This was a conscious reaction to the modern, online, perfect-existence, social media-ness of it all. Audio engineer Emily Wheatcroft-Snape was recommended to the band because of her ability to capture sounds with accuracy and precision - and she encapsulated the live band just as they had hoped.


Thematically, ‘And It Wants’ sees Ruddell clinging to optimism and joy while being subject to the existential nihilism of our current hypernormal, western reality. “Death is all through this record. The songs were born out of the feeling that there are no rules, that nothing matters, and that we all die. That we dance around the fact that death comes for us all, but we never really, truly, acknowledge it - it’s just too big or too heavy to have any kind of impact on our day to day existence. The intent is to provide a sonic backdrop to dance ecstatically, liberated, as the world around you burns. Find comfort and joy in things while you can, even as the end draws near and darkness begins to ruminate.”


‘And It Wants’ is out digitally, and on two exclusive vinyl variants via Flying Nun Records and Holiday Records on October 23rd.

id: Welcome Space Brothers - The Story Of Unarius-Vogelmorn Upstairs, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Story Of Unarius
long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as Archangel Uriel—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!



“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille



“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 



“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

Horn – Bright Green Dull Ache Vinyl Album Release
Horn celebrates the release of her third album, Bright Green Dull Ache, with an intimate Wellington house show featuring Silicon Tongue and Special Guests.
This special home-based performance will bring together three Wellington acts for an evening of live music and celebration around the release of Bright Green Dull Ache. The house-show setting offers a more intimate and personal environment for audiences to experience some of the new material live.
Bright Green Dull Ache is Horn’s third album, with its release on vinyl marking an important milestone in the project. The album was mixed by Abigail Macilquham and Warwick Donald, and mastered by James Goldsmith. Recorded at Mansfield Street Studios in Newtown, Wellington.
The Wellington house show will provide an opportunity to hear some new songs from Bright Green Dull Ache performed live in an intimate setting, alongside performances from Silicon Tongue and Special Guests. Vinyl copies of Bright Green Dull Ache will be available to purchase at the show, giving audiences the opportunity to take home a physical copy of the new release.

id: Delphine Dora (FR), Tamagawa (FR), Amy Jean Barnett-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Delphine Dora (FR), Tamagawa (FR), Amy Jean Barnett
long_description:
Pyramid Club is excited to present French pianist, organist, vocalist, improviser, and composer, Delphine Dora, alongside fellow countryman Tamagawa and Wellington's Amy Jean Barnett.
-
Born in Paris in 1980, Delphine Dora has cultivated a distinctive and intuitive musical language that bridges improvisation, folk, contemporary classical, experimental and electroacoustic music, as well as poetic expression. Her work, deeply anchored in the present moment, delves into altered temporalities and sensitive geographies, forming a resonant dialogue between improvisation and composition, the contemporary and the archaic, the poetic and the ineffable, the physicality of sound and the ethereal, the outer world and inner life. Encompassing pipe organ explorations, genre-blurring song forms, piano compositions, and site-specific improvisations, her performances take place in venues around the world, from underground experimental spaces to historic churches. The Wire magazine says Browsing through her labyrinthine discography is like opening a spiritualist’s cabinet: scattered over labels such as Fort Evil Fruit, Okarïna, three:four and Dora’s own imprint Wild Silence, her releases include countless joint efforts featuring artists such as Keiji Haino and Half Asleep. Shelves are filled with all sorts of music, ranging from avant garde adaptions of poetry to organ drones.
-
Tamagawa is the solo project of french guitarist Bertrand Gaude (Temple Solaire, Le Club des Gens Speciaux). Constructed in and around his apartment cell (from which he practically never goes out except to tour a bit, everywhere on the planet including more than 300 concerts in Europe, Japan and the United States), Tamagawa records alternating minimalist glittering guitars and analog synths. Aymeric Hainaux writes in Tamagawa's music there is an immense solitude, and in itself, silence takes the form of a (minor) key. Emotion is gradually forming in a succession of notes whose infinite purity doesn’t even allow us a beat of the eyelid.
-
Amy Jean Barnett is a composer and performer working with acoustic instruments, electronics and historical tuning systems. Drawing from minimalist and electroacoustic lineages, her music is patient and focused, balancing restraint with sustained resonance, evolving harmonic structures and subtle timbral variation. Attentive to the elusive details that emerge through close listening, her work explores the coexistence of continuity and impermanence. Recent projects include multichannel installations, instrumental scores and recorded works.

Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

name: Flyte
long_description:
Presented by Banished Music & The Tuning Fork, acclaimed indie band Flyte bring their signature blend of heartfelt lyricism and melodic craftsmanship to a special run of New Zealand shows this November, performing at Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Friday November 13 and Wellington’s San Fran on Saturday November 14.

Tickets will be available via presale from Wednesday 20 May at 10am NZST. The general public will then be able to secure their tickets from Friday 22 May at 10am NZST.

Flyte have earned widespread acclaim for their refined songwriting and emotionally resonant sound, with a catalogue that showcases their evolution from classic British guitar pop to more expansive and introspective arrangements. Their releases have been celebrated for their lyrical honesty and rich harmonies, cementing their place as one of the UK’s most compelling contemporary bands.

Kia ora, hola, olá!

You’re invited to the first Latin Market & Expo – Hutt Valley, a free community event celebrating Latin culture, food, products, services, businesses and local connection.

Join us for a vibrant day in Lower Hutt where the local community, Latin American families, small businesses, food vendors, makers, service providers and community organisations come together in one shared space.

Explore indoor expo stands, discover local and Latin-led businesses, enjoy an outdoor Latin food court, meet people from across the Hutt Valley, and experience a welcoming event designed for everyone — Latin, Kiwi, multicultural, families, friends, neighbours and anyone curious to connect with the Latin community.

This event is about more than a market. It is a community showcase: a place to celebrate culture, support local businesses, create new connections and make Latin American presence more visible in Hutt Valley.

Time: 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM
Location: The Dowse / James Coe Centre, Lower Hutt

Everyone is welcome — bring your family, invite your friends, and come along to enjoy food, culture, products, services and community connection.

name: Submarine - Wellington
long_description:
We’re going deep.

Hailing all the way from Berlin, Vault 9 is very proud to announce:

SUBMARINE

Wellington, you’re in for another night of deep, rolling Drum & Bass! Known for a sound that sits in the deep end of the genre, Submarine will bring you liquid melodies, halftime arrangements and minimal madness for a journey unlike anything that has blessed your ears. With an insane catalogue on labels such as 1985 Music, Demand Records and Flexout Audio, he’s well equipped to deliver a set that won’t be forgotten.

We’ve also hand-picked a support crew that, alongside Submarine, will take the night to another level: DXN, Louder, Intec, Pearly, Gunn, Zillah, Fe, Java all being hosted by Timmy P… Wellington’s finest. These selectas have been sculpted by the gods to bring you only the very best selections known to man, and they’ll ensure your legs are skanking with your bass faces on. All. Damn. Night.

As our very first international artist, we couldn’t be happier to show Submarine what Wellington’s made of. We’ve wanted to bring a headliner from overseas for a long time and are finally getting it done, with a producer whose sound fits our city’s vibe to a T!

The lineup is stacked, the date is set, and the venue is pumped. We’ll be delivering vibes that are deep, melodic and memorable. Even Eminem would tell you this opportunity comes once in a lifetime, so don’t miss it. Get your tickets ASAP!

Afters @ 38 Dixon Street

Friday 14 November 9pm - 3am

Tix via Humanitix (link in bio)

18+
